thunc 0.3.2 makes **agent runs on the Claude API steadier**, and **a trace that can't be written no longer costs the answer**. Two fixes from a stability review of 0.3.1; nothing else is new.

```bash
pip install --upgrade "thunc[watch]"
```

**Fixed**
- **An error the Claude API sends mid-reply is retried when asking again may fix it.** An overloaded, rate-limit, timeout or server error that arrives while a reply streams comes with the stream's HTTP status, 200, so thunc took it for a permanent error and the agent run failed. It's now retried like the same error arriving before the reply: twice, with a pause, as the docs say. A bad request, a bad key or a billing error still fails at once ([#68](https://github.com/Eltarras/thunc/pull/68)).
- **A trace file that can't be written warns instead of failing the call.** With `trace=` or `THUNC_TRACE` naming a folder that doesn't exist or a read-only file, every call and agent run raised the file's error: a successful call lost its answer, already paid for, and a failed one hid its own error. Now thunc warns once per path, and the call returns its value or raises its own error ([#68](https://github.com/Eltarras/thunc/pull/68)).

**Measured** (the same harness on 0.3.1 and 0.3.2, with only the API client or backend scripted)

| | 0.3.1 | 0.3.2 |
|---|---|---|
| 10-step agent runs that finish, 5% of requests failing mid-reply | 58.9% | 99.9% |
| The same, 10% failing | 33.4% | 98.8% |
| Calls and runs with an unwritable trace that end as with tracing off | 0/20 | 20/20 |
| Time per call with a working trace | 42.5–43.4 µs | 40.9–44.5 µs (no change) |

**Tested**
- Offline tests run on Python 3.10–3.14 on Ubuntu, and on Windows, with 12 new tests for these fixes: errors sent mid-reply, in the shape the SDK raises them, retried or not by their type, and calls and agent runs with a trace path that can't be written.

**Behavior changes**
- An agent run on the Claude API that met an overloaded, rate-limit, timeout or server error mid-reply now retries the step, so it can take a little longer instead of failing.
- A trace file that can't be written is a `RuntimeWarning`, once per path, instead of an `OSError` from the call. To make it an error again, turn the warning into one with `warnings.filterwarnings("error", "thunc could not write the trace")`.
- thunc-watch stays at 0.1.0.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Eltarras/thunc/compare/v0.3.1...v0.3.2
